rationale: C15 plausibly supplied a material drafting template. Both letters open by regretting circumstances that make resignation necessary, use the distinctive formulation that the President has no choice but to accept it, praise the official's competent and unselfish service, and close with wishes for whatever future work the official undertakes. C07 is also closely relevant because it concerns the resignation of the immediately preceding Secretary of Labor and contains parallel praise of the official's contribution to the Department, but its literal phrasing is less distinctive. C03 has the standard resignation-letter sequence but weaker direct overlap.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I deeply regret the necessity expressed in your letter ... compelling you to return to private life.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I regret very much the circumstances which make you feel it is necessary to submit your resignation
shared_material.explanation: Closely parallel opening language frames resignation as regrettable and compelled by circumstances.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have no course, however, but to respect your wishes, and to accept your resignation
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Under present circumstances, however, I feel I have no choice but to accept your resignation
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive near-verbatim formulation strongly indicates reusable language.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your patient skill and rich experience have been of unique value.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: carried out your duties with vigor, competence, and effectiveness
shared_material.explanation: Both follow acceptance with an appraisal of the departing official's effectiveness.

shared_material.child_excerpt: my warm wishes for a career of renewed distinction in whatever you undertake
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I wish you success and happiness in whatever future work you undertake
shared_material.explanation: The closing wishes share unusually close wording and the same future-work formulation.
